source_text: Sed ut hoc humanum, sic illud aliud, si putasset, non solum inhumanum, non solum ferum, verum etiam iniustum, non solum iniustum, verum etiam insanum, ut peccatum si nosset innasci, exprobraret suae aetatis hominibus vitia partus antiqui et ab his praeciperet abstinendum, quae innata credebat, atque cum interminatione praescriberet debere me ea deponere, quae ante habere coeperam, quam anima in corpus meum, in hunc vero mundum corpus intraret.
pass_a_gloss: But as this is human, so that other, if he had thought it, not only inhuman, not only wild, but also unjust, not only unjust but also insane, that if he knew sin to be inborn, he would reproach humans of his age with the vices of an ancient birth and would command that those things be abstained from which he believed inborn, and with a threatening would prescribe that I ought to lay down those things which I had begun to have before the soul entered into my body, but the body into this world.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS anima; Blaise human soul as image
LS abstineo; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: But just as this is human, the other position, if he had held it, would have been not merely inhuman and savage, but unjust—and not merely unjust, but insane. If he knew sin was inborn, he would be reproaching people of his own age with the faults of an ancient birth, commanding abstention from things he believed innate, and prescribing with threats that I must lay down things I had begun to possess before my soul entered my body and my body entered this world.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Opposite of iustitia; Julian refuses a God whose ordinances establish injustice.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
